issues.description: The problem description inconsistently refers to a method named getFeedingSound() for the concrete animals (Seal, Pig, Goat) while the UML and the rest of the specification define and expect an abstract method named messageOnFeed() in Animal. This naming mismatch can confuse students about which method to implement and which method will be used by the Farm/song logic and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either (a) update the problem statement (and any example/song placeholders) to refer to messageOnFeed() instead of getFeedingSound(), or (b) rename the abstract method in Animal (and corresponding implementations and template signatures) to getFeedingSound() everywhere. Prefer option (a) to match the UML and the existing solution implementation.

issues.description: The problem statement refers to the animal feeding behavior using two different method names: messageOnFeed() (in the UML and Part 1) and getFeedingSound() (in Part 2 and the feedAllAnimals description). The template/solution code uses messageOnFeed(). This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual method (the animal feeding sound) can confuse students about which method to implement/call and may lead to implementing the wrong identifier or failing tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across all artifacts. Update the problem statement to use messageOnFeed() everywhere (replace occurrences of getFeedingSound() with messageOnFeed()), or alternatively change the code to provide getFeedingSound() (and delegate messageOnFeed() to it). Preferably standardize on messageOnFeed() to match the UML and the solution implementation.
